summary: This program counts backwards, printing the numbers 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 on separate lines. It shows how a range can walk downwards instead of upwards.

lines.text: The three arguments to range are the start, the stop, and the step. Starting at 5 and stepping by -1 counts down, and because the stop value is never included, the sequence ends at 1 rather than 0.
The indented body runs once for each value the loop hands to i, so each countdown number appears on its own line.
